name: Milo Subscriptions – Subscriptions for WooCommerce and Recurring Payments
author: Milo Subscriptions

sections.description:
Milo Subscriptions is a free subscriptions plugin for WooCommerce, built on modern WordPress. The free core handles recurring billing, free trials, sign-up fees, and plan switching with proration. Customers manage their own plans in My Account. Mixed carts and the WooCommerce Blocks checkout work out of the box. Not running WooCommerce? A built-in standalone mode sells recurring plans on any WordPress site, with no store, products, or cart required.

The core plugin, completely free:

  • Subscription product type with daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom billing intervals
  • Free trials and one-time sign-up fees
  • Mixed carts – subscription products and one-off products in the same checkout
  • Plan switching with prorated charges and credits
  • Variable subscription products
  • Customer self-service portal in My Account: cancel, pause, resume, update payment method
  • WooCommerce Blocks checkout fully supported
  • Subscription Health Check that automatically scans for broken subscriptions (expired payment methods, stale gateway tokens, drifted renewal dates)
  • Built-in migrator that imports existing WooCommerce Subscriptions data
  • Modern admin with subscriptions that are sortable, filterable, and searchable
  • REST API for core subscription management (list, create, update, status, notes, renewals, bulk actions, and more)
  • HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) compatible
  • Standalone mode: sell subscriptions and recurring plans without WooCommerce (plans, subscribe blocks and shortcodes, a customer portal, and gateway webhooks)
  • Available in 17 languages, fully translation-ready (Arabic, Danish, German, Greek, Spanish, Finnish, French, Hebrew, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Turkish, Simplified Chinese)

Payments

Milo Subscriptions takes subscription payments through the free Milo Payments plugin. It connects PayPal, Stripe, Mollie, and Square in one admin. Already using another gateway, like Authorize.Net, Braintree, or GoCardless? The Any Gateway add-on lets subscriptions check out with any recurring-capable gateway you already have.

Sell subscriptions without WooCommerce (standalone mode)

No WooCommerce store? Milo Subscriptions runs on its own. Turn on standalone mode and take recurring payments on any WordPress site, with no products or cart. It is a complete way to sell recurring plans on WordPress without WooCommerce.

  • Create subscription plans with their own price, billing interval, and free trial
  • Add a subscribe button to any page with a block or shortcode
  • Recurring billing through Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, and Square (via the free Milo Payments plugin), driven by secure gateway webhooks
  • A customer portal where subscribers manage, pause, or cancel their plan
  • Subscription emails, analytics (MRR and active subscribers), and GDPR export and erase built in

Leave standalone mode off and Milo behaves like a classic WooCommerce subscriptions plugin. Same plugin, your choice.

42 premium add-ons, one ecosystem

Milo Subscriptions handles the fundamentals. When your store needs more, 42 premium add-ons cover the whole subscription journey, available individually or all together in the All Add-ons Bundle. Browse them from the in-plugin marketplace (Subscriptions > Add-ons) or on milosubscriptions.com.

Billing flexibility

  • Subscription Coupons – recurring discounts and prepayment incentives
  • All Products for Subscriptions – add a Subscribe & Save option to existing products
  • Payment Plans – split a purchase into a fixed number of installments
  • Trials Pro – free or paid trials with one-trial-per-customer protection
  • Scheduled Start Dates – customers pick when billing begins
  • Store Credit – balances that pay renewals automatically
  • Gift Cards – sell codes that redeem into store credit
  • Invoices – sequential invoice numbers, printable invoices, VAT field
  • Any Gateway – subscription checkout with any recurring-capable gateway
  • Stripe Bridge – recurring billing through the official WooCommerce Stripe gateway, made for WCS migrations

Retention and lifecycle

  • Failed Payment Retry – smart retry schedules that recover real revenue
  • Cancellation Flows – pause or discount offers before a cancellation goes through
  • Winback – automated come-back campaigns with one-click resubscribe
  • Onboarding – welcome email sequences that kill early churn
  • NPS – one-click satisfaction surveys, detractor alerts
  • Loyalty – points on every payment, redeemable on renewals
  • Compliance – consent proof, pre-renewal notices, one-click cancel links, audit trail

Growth and marketing

  • Referrals – subscriber referral links with two-sided rewards
  • Affiliates – partner program with recurring commissions on renewals
  • Social Proof – live subscriber counters and “someone just subscribed” toasts
  • Pricing Tables – current-plan-aware pricing tables as a block or shortcode
  • Waitlist – capacity-limited products with automatic FIFO invitations
  • Gifting – let customers buy subscriptions for someone else

Physical subscriptions and fulfillment

  • Box Builder – mix-and-match boxes customers fill and edit each cycle
  • Fulfillment – shipments screen, aggregated pick lists, packing slips, tracking
  • Stock Management – reserve inventory for active subscribers
  • Split Shipping – one subscription order, multiple addresses
  • Calendar – private renewal/delivery calendar feeds and a merchant schedule
  • Age Check – date-of-birth verification for age-restricted subscriptions

Access, teams, and community

  • Memberships – restrict content, products, and downloads by active subscription
  • Teams – one subscription, multiple seats, manager-invited members
  • Transfer – move a subscription to a new owner, history intact
  • Discord – automatic subscriber roles on your Discord server
  • Download Limits – cap downloadable file access by subscription status
  • Pass – QR member passes scanned at the door, verified live
  • License Server – sell software licenses with keys, activations, updates, and GitHub release sync

Insights and operations

  • Advanced Analytics – MRR, churn, LTV, retention cohorts, forecasts
  • Webhooks – signed event deliveries with retries for any integration
  • Slack – subscription events in your team channel as they happen
  • Milo TV – a live full-screen dashboard for the office TV
  • Gravity Forms – sell subscriptions through Gravity Forms
  • Digest – a periodic email summary of your subscription business

Learn more at milosubscriptions.com.

External Services

Milo Subscriptions connects to milosubscriptions.com, in two situations:

1. Anonymous usage tracking (opt-in, off by default).
If you enable “Usage tracking” in the plugin settings, Milo Subscriptions sends an anonymized weekly report to our website. This is disabled by default and never runs unless you turn it on. The report contains no personal data: plugin, WordPress, PHP, and WooCommerce versions; locale, currency, and store base country; a one-way hash of your site URL; aggregate subscription counts and MRR; the payment gateways and billing periods in use; and which Milo add-ons are active. It is sent once per week while enabled, and stops when you disable the setting.

2. Downloading the free Milo Payments plugin (on demand).
When you choose to install Milo Payments from the plugin’s admin, the plugin file is fetched from our website. This request only happens when you click to install and sends no data beyond a standard download request.

By using these features you agree to the milosubscriptions.com Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the milosubscriptions folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install via the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. For WooCommerce stores, run WooCommerce 8.0 or later. (Not required – Milo Subscriptions also runs in standalone mode without WooCommerce.)
  4. Go to Products → Add New and select Subscription as the product type.
  5. Configure the billing period, price, and optional trial in the Subscription tab.
  6. (Optional) Install the free Milo Payments plugin for a unified gateway admin, or use your existing gateway plugins.

No WooCommerce? Standalone mode: Enable Standalone mode in Milo Subscriptions → Settings, create a plan, then add a subscribe button to any page with the Milo block or shortcode. Recurring payments run through the free Milo Payments plugin (Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, Square), with no WooCommerce, products, or cart required.
sections.faq:
Is Milo Subscriptions really free?

Yes. The core plugin is free, listed on WordPress.org, and stays that way. Premium add-ons and the All Add-ons Bundle are sold separately at milosubscriptions.com.

Can I sell subscriptions without WooCommerce?

Yes. Milo Subscriptions includes a standalone mode that runs without WooCommerce installed. You create plans, add a subscribe button to any page with a block or shortcode, and take recurring payments through Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, or Square using the free Milo Payments plugin. Subscribers get a self-service portal, and you get subscription emails, analytics (MRR and active subscribers), and GDPR tools, all with no WooCommerce store, products, or cart. If you do run WooCommerce, leave standalone mode off and Milo works as a full WooCommerce subscriptions plugin instead.

How do customers subscribe in standalone mode?

You create a plan in Milo Subscriptions, then place a subscribe button on any page using the Milo block in the WordPress editor or a shortcode. When a customer subscribes, Milo collects payment through the free Milo Payments plugin and sets up the recurring schedule. Renewals are charged automatically and confirmed by secure gateway webhooks, with no WooCommerce cart or checkout involved.

Can I switch between standalone and WooCommerce mode?

Yes. The billing mode is a single setting. Run standalone on a site without WooCommerce, or leave it off and Milo behaves as a full WooCommerce subscriptions plugin. Standalone subscriptions and WooCommerce subscriptions are kept in their own records, so the mode you pick is the system that drives billing.

Does it work with WooCommerce Subscriptions?

Milo Subscriptions is a complete alternative to WooCommerce Subscriptions, not a companion plugin. It uses the same shop_subscription post type and a similar data model, which makes migrating in a clean operation.

Can I migrate from WooCommerce Subscriptions?

Yes. Milo ships with a built-in migrator that imports your existing subscriptions, customers, and billing schedules from WooCommerce Subscriptions. Saved payment methods come across too, with renewals routed through the free Milo Payments plugin: connect the same gateway account you already use (Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, or Square) and your existing tokens keep charging without customers re-entering their cards. The migrator checks during preflight that the matching Milo Payments gateway is connected to the right account before you start. The one exception is WooPayments: it keeps saved cards in its own managed account that no other gateway can charge, so those subscriptions are imported with billing paused and the customer re-confirms their card once (see the WooPayments FAQ below). Prefer to keep renewing through a different third-party gateway instead? Add the Any Gateway add-on. Most stores migrate in an afternoon. See the migration guide for the full walkthrough.

I use WooPayments. Can I migrate without interruption?

Your subscriptions, schedules, customers, and history migrate normally. Saved cards are the exception. WooPayments stores cards in its own managed Stripe account, which your store has no direct API access to, so no other gateway (Milo included) can charge them. This is true of any move away from WooPayments, not something specific to Milo. Those subscriptions are imported with billing paused, and each customer re-confirms their card once (a one-click secure link) before their next renewal. If you instead pay through the official Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, or Square gateways, your saved cards transfer and renewals continue without interruption.

Can I export my data, or leave Milo later?

Yes, and easily. Your subscriptions are stored as standard WooCommerce shop_subscription orders with _milo_* meta, not in a proprietary format. From the Subscriptions screen, the Export button downloads every subscription as JSON or CSV: status, schedule, billing terms, totals, line items, customer, addresses, payment-method identifiers, and meta. Saved cards keep working with any plugin charging the same gateway account, and the WooCommerce Subscriptions migration is reversible. See “Your data is yours” in the docs for the full guarantee.

Which payment gateways are supported?

The free core processes payments through the companion free Milo Payments plugin, which connects PayPal, Stripe, Mollie, and Square through one unified admin. To check out with a different gateway you already have (the official Stripe gateway, Authorize.Net, Braintree, GoCardless, or any other gateway that supports recurring tokens), add the Any Gateway add-on.

Is it HPOS compatible?

Yes. Milo Subscriptions declares full compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage.

Does it work with WooCommerce Blocks checkout?

Yes. The block-based checkout works out of the box for subscription products, including mixed carts.

How is the Subscription Health Check different from a regular WooCommerce report?

The Health Check scans every active subscription on a nightly schedule (and on demand) and flags issues that would otherwise surface as customer support tickets later: payment methods that have expired at the gateway, customer IDs that no longer resolve, renewal dates that have drifted out of sync. You see problems before customers email you.

What’s the difference between Milo Subscriptions and the All Add-ons Bundle?

Milo Subscriptions (this plugin) is the free main plugins. The Bundle ($149/year) unlocks every premium add-on we ship – currently 12 add-ons including Memberships, Gifting, Failed Payment Retry, and Advanced Analytics – plus every future paid add-on for as long as the license is active. Paid add-ons are covered by our Refund Policy.

Where can I report a bug or request a feature?

Open a thread in the WordPress.org support forum for this plugin, or email support@milosubscriptions.com.
sections.changelog:
1.8.7

  • Fixed: admin links (Configure payments, Open wizard, Add product, Back to WP Admin) pointed at a root relative /wp-admin/ path, so they returned the theme’s “Page not found” on installs where WordPress lives in a subdirectory, such as the Bedrock and roots.io stack. They now use the admin URL WordPress reports.
  • Fixed: the migration progress bar could display more than 100% after an out-of-band (CLI) migration.
  • Fixed: a PHP deprecation notice (strip_tags on a null title) on the setup wizard screen with PHP 8.1+.

1.8.6

  • Fixed: the Attributes tab was hidden on regular (non-subscription) products, including plain variable and simple products.

1.8.5

  • Fixed: the “Used for variations” checkbox stayed hidden on variable subscription products after WooCommerce’s attribute AJAX renders, blocking variation generation.

1.8.4

  • Added: Milo Stripe Bridge in the add-ons marketplace (catalog at 42): keep the official WooCommerce Stripe gateway, saved cards, and mandates when migrating from WooCommerce Subscriptions.

1.8.3

  • Added: Stripe Bridge, Pass, and Digest add-on cards in the marketplace (42 add-ons); unique colors restored on the Any Gateway and Webhooks cards.

1.8.2

  • Fixed: fatal error on every wp-admin page when WooCommerce is not installed (standalone mode): the first-run wizard’s existing-data check called WooCommerce functions unconditionally; it now falls back to the standalone subscriptions table.

1.8.2

  • Fixed: the settings snackbar no longer overlaps the admin shell frame.
  • Added: the milo_subscriptions_user_has_active_subscription filter, so add-ons (such as the upcoming Teams add-on) can grant active-subscriber access to users who inherit it rather than owning a subscription directly.
  • Added: time-released (drip) downloads for WooCommerce downloadable products.
  • Added: Teams, Cancellation Flows, Box Builder, Elementor Connector, Webhooks, Referrals, Loyalty, Invoices, Payment Plans, Trials Pro, Pricing Tables, Winback, Waitlist, NPS, Store Credit, Slack, Gift Cards, Onboarding, Affiliates, Fulfillment, Compliance, Social Proof, Transfer, Discord, Calendar, Age Check, and Milo TV add-ons in the marketplace.

1.8.1

  • Fixed: a subscription whose first payment is $0 (for example a 100% coupon) is no longer cancelled when WooCommerce’s unpaid-order stock cron cancels the still-pending parent order. Subscription parent orders are now exempt from that cron, and the order _subscription_ids list no longer starts with an empty string.
  • Changed: plan switching now prorates by direction. An upgrade charges only the prorated difference immediately (it used to overcharge close to the full new price); a downgrade charges nothing now and credits the overpaid remainder to the next renewal; a same-price switch charges nothing.
  • Changed: switching a plan no longer re-charges the plan sign-up fee (it is a one-time onboarding charge the customer already paid). Opt in via the milo_subscriptions_charge_signup_fee_on_switch filter for plans with a genuine per-switch setup cost.
  • Fixed: switching a plan during a free trial no longer applies a proration credit (nothing has been charged for the current period yet). The switch still bills the new plan at the trial end.
  • Added: standalone plan downloads can be time-released (drip). Each file has an “available after N days” setting in the plan editor; it unlocks that many days after the subscription starts, and the account/shortcode list shows a “Available on ” label until then.

1.8.0

  • Added: standalone plans can offer downloadable Media Library files, gated to active subscribers and listed with the [milo_subscriptions_downloads] shortcode.
  • Added: a unified “My Account” area for standalone subscribers (subscription details + downloads + licenses), available as the [milo_subscriptions_account] shortcode and the My Account block.
  • Added: standalone plans can grant a license via the Milo License Server, issued to active subscribers and revoked on cancellation; license keys appear in the account area.
  • Added: developer hooks on the standalone download endpoint (milo_subscriptions_download_allowed filter, milo_subscriptions_download_served action) so add-ons can gate or meter downloads (e.g. per-period quotas).
  • Fixed: add-on settings sections with multiple fields now have proper spacing between fields.
  • Added: a per-plan meta layer so add-ons can attach settings to standalone plans (milo_subscriptions_plan_fields filter renders fields in the plan editor; milo_subscriptions_get_plan_meta() reads them).

1.7.0

  • Fixed: the Products admin list now spans the full width like the other list screens (it was capped at 1200px).
  • Fixed: removed a dormant, mismatched internal data-store mapping for subscriptions (hardening; no behavior change).
  • Added: subscription fields now round-trip through the WooCommerce product CSV import and export.

short_description: Free WooCommerce subscriptions and recurring payments, or standalone without WooCommerce. Trials, switching, self-service, and migration tools.

Milo Subscriptions is a free subscriptions plugin for WooCommerce, built on modern WordPress. The free core handles recurring billing, free trials, sign-up fees, and plan switching with proration. Customers manage their own plans in My Account. Mixed carts and the WooCommerce Blocks checkout work out of the box. Not running WooCommerce? A built-in standalone mode sells recurring plans on any WordPress site, with no store, products, or cart required.

The core plugin, completely free:

  • Subscription product type with daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom billing intervals
  • Free trials and one-time sign-up fees
  • Mixed carts – subscription products and one-off products in the same checkout
  • Plan switching with prorated charges and credits
  • Variable subscription products
  • Customer self-service portal in My Account: cancel, pause, resume, update payment method
  • WooCommerce Blocks checkout fully supported
  • Subscription Health Check that automatically scans for broken subscriptions (expired payment methods, stale gateway tokens, drifted renewal dates)
  • Built-in migrator that imports existing WooCommerce Subscriptions data
  • Modern admin with subscriptions that are sortable, filterable, and searchable
  • REST API for core subscription management (list, create, update, status, notes, renewals, bulk actions, and more)
  • HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) compatible
  • Standalone mode: sell subscriptions and recurring plans without WooCommerce (plans, subscribe blocks and shortcodes, a customer portal, and gateway webhooks)
  • Available in 17 languages, fully translation-ready (Arabic, Danish, German, Greek, Spanish, Finnish, French, Hebrew, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Turkish, Simplified Chinese)

Payments

Milo Subscriptions takes subscription payments through the free Milo Payments plugin. It connects PayPal, Stripe, Mollie, and Square in one admin. Already using another gateway, like Authorize.Net, Braintree, or GoCardless? The Any Gateway add-on lets subscriptions check out with any recurring-capable gateway you already have.

Sell subscriptions without WooCommerce (standalone mode)

No WooCommerce store? Milo Subscriptions runs on its own. Turn on standalone mode and take recurring payments on any WordPress site, with no products or cart. It is a complete way to sell recurring plans on WordPress without WooCommerce.

  • Create subscription plans with their own price, billing interval, and free trial
  • Add a subscribe button to any page with a block or shortcode
  • Recurring billing through Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, and Square (via the free Milo Payments plugin), driven by secure gateway webhooks
  • A customer portal where subscribers manage, pause, or cancel their plan
  • Subscription emails, analytics (MRR and active subscribers), and GDPR export and erase built in

Leave standalone mode off and Milo behaves like a classic WooCommerce subscriptions plugin. Same plugin, your choice.

External Services

Milo Subscriptions connects to milosubscriptions.com, in two situations:

1. Anonymous usage tracking (opt-in, off by default).
If you enable “Usage tracking” in the plugin settings, Milo Subscriptions sends an anonymized weekly report to our website. This is disabled by default and never runs unless you turn it on. The report contains no personal data: plugin, WordPress, PHP, and WooCommerce versions; locale, currency, and store base country; a one-way hash of your site URL; aggregate subscription counts and MRR; the payment gateways and billing periods in use; and which Milo add-ons are active. It is sent once per week while enabled, and stops when you disable the setting.

2. Downloading the free Milo Payments plugin (on demand).
When you choose to install Milo Payments from the plugin’s admin, the plugin file is fetched from our website. This request only happens when you click to install and sends no data beyond a standard download request.
